adjudicated.jp: 「実はな、俺は記憶ソーシツだ」
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "Truth is, I got some memories missing."
comments: Odd emphasis on what should normally read "memory loss". Interesting that he goes into what is almost certainly narcolepsy, and the first character that comes out is Yutaka, who does have narcolepsy. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 唐突に、ヤツは言った。
adjudicated.en: Out of the blue the guy said that.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「主人公みたいだな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Like a main character innit."
comments: Ah, but our protagonist has perfect recollection. Just watch how he consciously remembers who Shinkawa is! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says only that he resembles a protagonist. It does not add a specifically British tag.

adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「なんでもない。忘れてくれ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Nothing, nothing. Just forget it."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 新川は語った。
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa spoke.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 少年期の記憶がないこと。
adjudicated.en: He has no memories of the time he was a boy,
comments: This works better flowing with the above, but with NVL that's not happening.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 先端恐怖症であること。
adjudicated.en: he has a phobia of things with pointed ends,
comments: Trypanophobia is a rare/uncommon term, common would be fear of needles. However... the term 先端 is often used for the dickhead in sex scenes. Compare Sakuraba's impotence, and there you go: this has nothing to do with needles, and it's purely sexual. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 森の暗がりに病的な恐怖を感じること。
adjudicated.en:
and the darkness of the woods makes him feel
a morbid fear.
comments: but I thought Morbid Manor was a level in-GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: なにかがあったのだ。昔。
adjudicated.en: Something had happened. A long time ago.
comments: See CCC3003 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: けど内容は知らないのだという。
adjudicated.en: But what, exactly, he doesn't know.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 霧の両親も教えてはくれなかったらしい。
adjudicated.en: Kiri's parents didn't seem to want to tell him.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says Kiri's parents apparently did not tell him. The English changes the completed refusal or omission into an inferred lack of desire.

highlights.text: didn't seem to want to tell him

adjudicated.jp: そして新川豊に家族がいないこと。
adjudicated.en:
And then, Shinkawa Yutaka spoke of how he is
without family.
comments: This adaptation wouldn't be needed if the first sentence flowed with the rest... curse this NVL segment for5seconds! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: This is another fact in the narrator's list: Yutaka has no family. The English invents a speech act by Shinkawa and shifts the past account into present tense.

highlights.text:
Shinkawa Yutaka spoke of how he is
without family

adjudicated.jp: 全ては闇の中。
adjudicated.en: All is in darkness.
comments: But Taichi can see through it. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: そしてついには、霧とともに群青送り。
adjudicated.en:
And then, in the end, he was sent to Gunjou
together with Kiri.
comments: Awww, don't just use "soshite" twice in a row... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Gunjou is a conventional ASCII representation of 群青's long final vowel. Omitting a macron is a romanization-style choice, not a source-bound translation error.

adjudicated.jp: 「……むぐむぐ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...munch, munch."
comments: This reminds me, he actually IS saying "munch munch", these are not SFX. The Japanese don't eat with SFX; they actually do say 'mugu mugu'. I either read it on Wikipedia or was told by the guy in the padded cell next to mine, so you know it's reliable. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺はピザを貪り食いながら聞いた。
adjudicated.en: I listened to all that while greedily devouring a pizza.
comments: His dontgiveashit level is in the upper reaches of 99%. This is very intentional. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: デリバリーしたピザだった。
adjudicated.en: It was a delivery pizza.
comments: DoCheSpe? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 当時、俺は非常に裕福であり、昼食は出前を取っていた。
adjudicated.en: Those days I was uncommonly affluent, therefore I had lunch delivered.
comments: Part 6, Taichi the Failed Speculator -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 基本的に心の治療という名目もあってか、群青での校則はあってなきに等しい。
adjudicated.en: Basically, with the pretext of healing the heart, Gunjou's school regulations are next to ignorable.
comments: PCP CCB0004C
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says the school rules at Gunjou are virtually nonexistent, partly under the pretext of mental treatment. The English says existing rules are merely ignorable and calques mental care as healing the heart. Gunjou itself is an acceptable ASCII long-vowel spelling and is not part of the error.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that, partly under the pretext of mental treatment, the school's rules are virtually nonexistent.

highlights.text: school regulations are next to ignorable

adjudicated.jp: ピザを取るのを止めたら、情緒不安定になるかも知れないからだ。
adjudicated.en: If I was prevented from having my pizza, I might just become emotionally unstable.
comments: So if he were to wear a girl's uniform and a wig and occasionally pretend to be a year older and in Misato's class, who'd stop him? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 治療という名目で人を隔離しているこの学校は、自意識さえあれば無法地帯だった。
adjudicated.en: The mere possession of self-awareness made a lawless space of this school designed to isolate people with the pretext of medical treatment.
comments: See CCA0021, CCA0007. Besides the meta (hi, trolled ones!), it's Gunjou that allows him to stay like this. I think the effect Tanaka's going with this concept of 'self-awareness' is that (sadly demonstrated) idea that the handlers of a nuthouse can't tell the insane ones from normal ones that were to be put in there by mistake. It's true because I'm totally sane and I was put in here by mistake so GET ME OUT OF HERE NOW DAMN GUAAAAAAARDJDSPGWE-GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says the school was a lawless zone for anyone still possessing a sense of self. The English makes possession of self-awareness the cause that transformed the school.

highlights.text: The mere possession of self-awareness made a lawless space of this school

adjudicated.jp: ……孤島の牢獄めいて。
adjudicated.en: ...it's like an island prison.
comments: See below, Kiri's talk about islands. The penitentiary of a hellish real world, as well as the thing about it being segregated from the outside by mountains. Laterally, it's Japan, as an island country. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「うーむ、そうだったか。記憶ソーシツ。うーむ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Hmmm, that's how it is. Memories missing. Hmmm."
comments: Sounds a bit like he's ridiculing him. Of course. He remembers. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺は熟考した。そして、
adjudicated.en: I gave it deep consideration. And then,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ＯＫ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Okieh!"
comments: Ibidem -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source is the English loan 'OK.' The invented eye-dialect spelling adds a voice not encoded by it.

adjudicated.jp: 「そうか……まあそういうと思ったがな……」
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "Right... well I thought, you know..."
adjudicated.assessment: Shinkawa says he figured Taichi would say that. The English omits the predicted speech and turns it into a vague act of thinking.

adjudicated.jp: 「俺は記憶ソーシツの新川を肯定するぞ。けど記憶喪失でない新川はご免被る」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I'll be positive on Shinkawa who has memories missing. But Shinkawa without memory loss is too unpleasant to accept."
comments: "I'll forgive you if you have memory loss, but if you don't, I won't". He may actually be consciously remembering at this point. He's lying to himself, however, see CCC3026, or rather, he's stating what he should do but won't, see CCC3030. Rules followed in the outwards, not in the depth, like Misato does, and as is his wont as a fallen human. Also, "I go well with Shinkawa with memory loss, but I don't with the one without memory loss". -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says he accepts the amnesiac Shinkawa but wants no part of a version without amnesia. The English uses the nonidiomatic 'positive on' and invents unpleasantness as the reason for refusal.

adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "......"
adjudicated.assessment: The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

adjudicated.jp: そんな気怠い空間に、霧が来た。
adjudicated.en: And in that listless space came Kiri.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「また二人でつるんでる」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "You two mate-ing again."
comments: So odd she'd use that term. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: つるむ means the two are hanging out together again. 'Mate-ing' is a malformed coinage that suggests sex or animal breeding.

adjudicated.jp: 「霧ちんだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Oh, Kiri-chin."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……霧ちんって呼ばないでください」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...please do not call me 'Kiri-chin'."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「だって霧ちんじゃん」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But you're Kiri-chin ain'tcha."
comments: 切り賃? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese makes a blunt colloquial assertion but does not encode this specifically dialectal English tag.

adjudicated.jp: 「霧です」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Just Kiri."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「じゃ霧」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Kiri then."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「呼び捨てにしないでください！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Please do not call me without honorific!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「どうしろと」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Make up your mind!"
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi asks what form of address she wants him to use. The English instead accuses her of indecision and orders her to resolve it.

adjudicated.jp: 「なあ豊？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Right, Yutaka?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.
The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 寝ていた。
adjudicated.en: He fell asleep.
comments: So damn meta. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says they discover him already asleep. The English depicts the event of falling asleep at that moment.

adjudicated.jp: 「すぐ寝るな、コイツ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Quick to sleep this guy."
comments: ONIIIIIIIIII-CHAAAAAAN WAKE UP -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese remarks that he falls asleep quickly. The English uses an adjective phrase before an unintegrated subject noun phrase.

adjudicated.jp: 「……昔からそうなんです」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...he has been like this since a long time ago."
comments: That "long time ago" again, see CCC3003. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: English uses 'for' with a duration: 'for a long time.'

adjudicated.jp: 「後遺症みたいなものらしくて……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "They seem to be something like after effects..."
comments: ITS YOUR FIRST DAY OF SCHOOL AT NEKO ACADEMY -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese calls the sleepiness something like a singular aftereffect. The English uses a plural pronoun without an antecedent and splits the compound 'aftereffects.'

highlights.text: They seem to be something like after effects

adjudicated.jp: 「ああ、例の記憶喪失ってやつ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, like how he has memory loss, then."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……豊に聞いたんですか」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...did Yutaka tell you?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「今さっき」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Just now."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「そうですか……信頼されてるんですね」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "So he did... that means you are trusted then."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「って？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Wha-?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「前の学校で、友達なんていませんでしたから。兄にも私にも」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Because, at our previous school we did not have friends. Neither I nor Ani."
comments: Unclear if Kiri and Yutaka went to the same school, or if the two were simply in the same conditions.
adjudicated.assessment: 兄 means her older brother. The English leaves it as an unexplained Japanese kinship term instead of translating it.

adjudicated.jp: よくあることだった。
adjudicated.en: That happened frequently,
comments: ONIiIiIiIiIiIiIiIiIiIiIiIiIi-CHAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAN -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 特に適応試験の結果は、よく漏れた。
adjudicated.en: especially since the results of the Conformity Test were frequently leaked.
comments: Your Tax Dollars At Work. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「友達だった人にも、裏切られて……誰も信用できなくなって……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Even the people who were friends betrayed us... we could no longer trust anyone..."
comments: See CCB0023. So easy to manipulate. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「誰も傷つけてないのに、みんなから傷つけられて」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "We did not hurt anyone, but still everybody hurt us."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「そして牙を剥くこともある」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "And then you went and bared your fangs."
comments: Referring to CCC3004 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese generalizes that victims may sometimes bare their fangs in response. The English assigns the action specifically to Kiri, shifts it into completed past, and adds reproachful 'went and.'

highlights.text: you went and bared your fangs

adjudicated.jp: 「攻撃されたら、身を守るのが当然じゃないですか」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "If you are attacked, is it not natural you would protect yourself?"
comments: Necessarily referring to him, see below. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「そういう考え方もある」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "That is one way of thinking, yes."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「けど身を守った猛獣は、撃ち殺されるのが世の常なんだよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But in this world, it's ordinary for wild beasts that defend themselves to be shot to death."
comments: Kiri's crossbow is a hunting weapon as well. Hypocrite much? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……人間じゃないですか」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...are you not human?"
comments: Careful now: different from his usual taunt, "you are not a person". She wondering why he would even consider not defending himself from someone who'd shoot him to death. Interesting foreshadowing, on this. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri protests that the supposedly wild beasts are human beings. The English instead asks whether Taichi himself is human.

adjudicated.jp: 低く、霧は吐いた。
adjudicated.en: So spat out Kiri, tone lowering.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says Kiri spits the words out in a low voice. The English uses an archaic inversion and makes her tone an ungoverned progressive fragment.

highlights.text: So spat out Kiri, tone lowering.

adjudicated.jp: 義憤。
adjudicated.en: Righteous indignation.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 現代を生きるには、霧はまっすぐにすぎた。
adjudicated.en: Kiri was far too straightforward to live in modern times.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「中にはね……本当に人じゃないのもいるんだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Inside here... truly, there's something not of the person."
comments: THIS is where her "you're not a person" will come from. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says some among them truly are no longer human. The English substitutes a place called 'inside here,' changes people to one thing, and produces the non-English phrase 'not of the person.'

highlights.text: Inside here... truly, there's something not of the person.

adjudicated.jp: 「たまにさ、周囲の人間のこと、どうでもいいって思っちゃうことってない？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Every once in a while, when you think about the people around you, don't you find yourself thinking they are sort of, like, irrelevant?"
comments: Thinking others irrelevant is not necessarily about thinking them worthless; it's about not thinking them as worth paying attention to, see CCB2006. It's more hinting that Taichi's simply pretending no one is there. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.
The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「俺はたまにある。たまにね。けど……完全にそうなったらおしまいだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I do, at times. At times, mind you. But... if I became completely like that, I'd be done for."
comments: Completeness, see below. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「頑張って生きないとな。少しでも奴らに尻尾を振って、あの普通の人とかいう連中に、媚びをうってでもさ……生きんと」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I just do my best to live. I wag my tail a bit to those people that call themselves normal, launch myself into flattery a bit to them... I gotta live."
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says he must work to survive even if that means wagging his tail and currying favor with so-called normal people. The English turns necessity into a current habit and says he 'launches' himself into flattery.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I just do my best to live. I wag my tail a bit to those people that call themselves normal, launch myself into flattery a bit to them... I gotta live."

adjudicated.jp: 「それで変な行動を？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Is that why you act so weird?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「さあ……考えたこともないや」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Dunno... never really gave it much thought."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……君もそうなんだぞ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...you're also like that."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Eh... me... as well?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「生存したかろうが」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You wanna live, don't you."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「わたしは……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "I..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「わたしは」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "I...!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 顔を伏せる。自分を抱く。
adjudicated.en: She lowers her face. And hugs herself.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「世界が恐くてたまらない、です」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "The world is unbearably frightening, yes."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「どんなところが？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "What part of it?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……悪意が」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...the malice."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「みんなの悪意が……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Everybody's malicious..."
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri identifies everyone's malice as what frightens her. The English instead directly characterizes every person as malicious.

adjudicated.jp: 「誰も……優しくない……優しさが少ない……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "No one... no kindness... not a shred of kindness..."
comments: "わたし、それだけでじゅうぶん。とっても優しくしてもらってるよ……" -GHS

adjudicated.jp: 震える。
adjudicated.en: She's shaking.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: そう。
adjudicated.en: Yes.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 彼女もまた、望んでここに来たわけでない。
adjudicated.en: She, herself, is not here because she has wished it.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says she did not come there by choice. The English mixes present location with present perfect wishing in a nonidiomatic causal construction.

highlights.text: is not here because she has wished it

adjudicated.jp: ここに来るしかなかった。
adjudicated.en: She was given no choice but to come here.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 国はそう定め給うた。
adjudicated.en: The country has so decreed,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 逆らうことは許されない。
adjudicated.en: and opposition is not tolerated.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……人間なんて、なくなる時にはあっさりなくなるって思ってます……だって、世界にはほとんど何もないから……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...I think that humans, when they depart, will just vanish like that... because in this world there is nearly nothing."
comments: Their death, their total disappeareance... the end of the world. This is part of how Taichi's Settei will be constructed. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri says humanity or human beings can disappear with shocking ease when the time comes. 'Depart' reframes this as individual death or leave-taking and the future tense makes it a prediction.

highlights.text: humans, when they depart, will just vanish like that

adjudicated.jp: 「きっと『何もない』方が多いんです。『なにかある』方は、ちょっとだけなんです！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "I am sure, there is Nothing in so much. In just so little is there Anything!"
comments: People, places, everything. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri says the realm of nothingness is surely much larger and the realm where something exists only a little. The English uses two ungrammatical inversions and fails to make the comparative relation intelligible.

highlights.text: there is Nothing in so much. In just so little is there Anything!

adjudicated.jp: 「いつ押し流されてしまうかもわからないって……思って」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "And we won't know when we will be washed away... I think."
comments: Perfectly predicted... but is it a prediction, or a self-fulfilling prophecy? The idea of the Big Wave continues the idea of the present day being allegorical for post-flood Earth, the lack of timeline is consistent with Matthew 24:38-39. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「その……ＳＦみたいな、人類滅亡とか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Sort of... an SF-like thing, the Fall of Mankind?"
comments: See CCC0016A, CCB0002. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「そういうのとは違って……そういう理由があるのとは違って……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "It is different from that... it is different in how there is a reason in that..."
comments: IOW, if this were sci-fi, there'd be some explanation. Troll 'em readers... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri says this differs from scenarios where there is an identifiable cause. The English stacks two locative 'in' phrases and does not state the contrast clearly.

highlights.text: it is different in how there is a reason in that

adjudicated.jp: 「夢から覚めたみたいに」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "This will be like waking up from a dream."
comments: This might as well be a direct quote from C.S. Lewis. More importantly, Taichi does a lot of dreaming... like right now. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri makes an atemporal comparison to waking from a dream. The English invents a future event and an explicit subject.

adjudicated.jp: 「いがみあってばかりで、こわいだけなのに……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "If all is quarreling, then everything is scary..."
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri says people do nothing but quarrel and that this is merely frightening. The English changes the statement into an ungrammatical conditional.

highlights.text: If all is quarreling, then everything is scary

adjudicated.jp: 「けどある日、突然すべてがなくなって……ちっぽけな世界で……もし自分ひとりが取り残されたらって考えると……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "But one day, all of a sudden everything will be no more... and I keep thinking, what if I was the only one that will be left behind... in that tiny worthless world..."
comments: Bah, don'tcha worry. That stuff's apocryphal. That's why Tanaka's a clever clever troll: those who don't look will think it some unexplained irrelevant sci-fi thing; those who look will think it Rapture, as humanity apparently up and vanishes; only those who look close enough will recognize it's the Great Flood except with Denpa instead of the actual waves. There's no being Left Behind after the Rapture here; there's no Rapture at all, as this is strictly pre-Apocalypse. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: ちっぽけ means tiny or puny. The English adds the distinct judgment that the world is worthless.

adjudicated.jp: 「わたし……わたしは……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "I... I'd..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「佐倉霧」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Sakura Kiri."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 呼び戻す。
adjudicated.en: I call her back.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 沈みかけていた表情にさっと色がさす。
adjudicated.en: Color sprung quickly in that face that had sunk into depression.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese metaphor says color returns to her expression as it is sinking. The English diagnoses the face as having sunk into depression and uses past perfect.

highlights.text: face that had sunk into depression

adjudicated.jp: 「あ……すいません……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Ah... apologies..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「悪意も恐い、一人も恐い……か」

comments: Dilemma. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.
The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「座ったら、ピザも食ってよし」

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "......"
adjudicated.assessment: The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...huh."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ゆるゆる座る。ピザには手をつけない。
adjudicated.en: She slowly sits down. She does not lay hand on the pizza.
comments: Japanese pizza, *shudder* -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English singular count noun requires a determiner or possessive: 'lay a hand on.'

adjudicated.jp: 感情の揺り戻し。
adjudicated.en: It's emotional swingback.
adjudicated.assessment: Emotional swingback is unusual English, but swingback transparently conveys the emotional reversal or rebound expressed by 揺り戻し. The wording is stylistically awkward rather than a confirmed source-side error.
adjudicated.remedy: No source-bound correction required; emotional rebound would be more idiomatic.

adjudicated.jp: 少しぼんやりしていた。
adjudicated.en: She was just a bit out of it.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「挙げ句の果てに流刑地に送られたっと」

comments: On the moon of Rura Penthe? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The fixed phrase is 'to top it all off.'

adjudicated.jp: 「……流刑地なんですか、ここ」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...so is this a penal colony, then?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says people able to feed themselves eat here and there around the room. The English literalizes independent ability as physical strength and makes ぽつぽつ modify the incremental manner of eating.

highlights.text: by their own strength were eating, bit by bit

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says they are self-contained or complete alone as an existing state. The English turns this into a process of becoming.

adjudicated.assessment: 齟齬 means frictions, mismatches, or misunderstandings. The rare plural 'discordances' is a technical calque rather than natural English for interpersonal conflict.

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: Standard English requires the infinitive marker: 'ought to be.'

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "..."

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Ah... eating things that other people have touched, I just cannot..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「潔癖性なんだ」

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You've also androphobia?"

adjudicated.assessment: The English question is missing the verb 'got' or 'have.'

adjudicated.jp: 「あ、こっちのは、別に……ただなんとなくで……男の人って……不潔だから」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Ah, not that, not really... it's just that somehow... males are... unclean, that's all."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「むちゃくちゃ言うな、おまえ」

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

highlights.text: generates withering in times of peace

adjudicated.jp: ……今のように。
adjudicated.en: ...like now.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

highlights.text: I'm happy and I shouldn't be

comments: This is what readers are supposed to think is Taichi's problem with Yutaka, at least until the reveal. And then they're supposed to forget that it changes nothing, and this is STILL Taichi's problem with Yutaka. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says he cannot steal Yutaka's future wife. The English adds physical or coercive force.

adjudicated.jp: 「あの、さっきの話ですけど……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Uhm, but, about what we were talking about before..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「悪意はないのかも知れないですけど……この学校は……なんだか『何もない』部分が広い気がして……話しかけても、誰も答えてくれないし」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Maybe there is no malice, but... somehow I feel that the parts with Nothing here are vast... even if you get close and talk to someone, they don't reply."
adjudicated.assessment: 話しかける means addressing or speaking to someone. The English adds physical approach as a separate action.

adjudicated.jp: 「そりゃ別に無視してるわけじゃない。法則が違うんだよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well now, it's not like they're really ignoring you. The laws are just different."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

comments: metal gear??? Either that or Tanaka's calling people who write like that as writing as/for children. If so I can't disagree. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: こっちが本当の霧だと悟った。

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese tentatively says that their channels do not intersect. The English introduces a second-person reflexive object, turns the relation into inability, and uses 'Cross' as an ungrammatical infinitive.

highlights.text: there is no way to make yourselves Cross

I can: SYMBOLISM!!! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「霧ちんも俺も、ベースの精神状態はノーマルだからさ。ノーマルじゃないベースのやつとは規格が違うわけだ」

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: 会話は成立する means communication or conversation can take place. English speakers do not normally 'construct conversations' in this sense.

adjudicated.jp: 「……どうやって……そんな法則を……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...how do you learn... these rules..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「観察力があれば。そうだな……たとえば」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Powers of observation are needed. Right, then... for example."
comments: He's also stating laterally what's needed to understand Cross Channel. Damn but Tanaka must have been laughing himself silly at writing this stuff. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: In context, Powers of observation are needed is a defensible pragmatic restatement of the condition if one has powers of observation. It makes the requirement explicit but does not reverse the argument or introduce a materially different criterion.
adjudicated.remedy: No source-bound correction required; If you're observant would follow the Japanese syntax more closely.

adjudicated.jp: 手近な席に座っている暗そうな眼鏡の女子のもとに。

comments: Ambiguous. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese describes a gloomy-looking girl with glasses. 'With ... mood dark' is not an English attributive construction.

highlights.text: a girl with glasses and mood dark

adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that she and Taichi actually have an established trading relationship. The English uses an object pronoun as subject and changes the standing arrangement into a future transaction.

highlights.text: Her and I will, in fact, be trading.

The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「とまあこのように」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "And, well, sort of like this."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...what was that now?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The English omits the article in 'is the foundation/basis' and strands the qualifier 'for her' as a fragment.

adjudicated.jp: 「あとは自分の世界だけでいい。だから半径３０センチ外の出来事には、関心が薄いんだ」

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「サヴァン症候群的な面もある。単純計算が異常にできる。あと数百年先のカレンダーの日にちと曜日をぴたりと即答する」

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「当然」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Naturally."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: Kiri says that even if there is no malice, she still hates or rejects such a state. The English turns her emotional refusal into a claim about correctness.

adjudicated.jp: 「だって……人がいるのに……一人一人が絶海の孤島みたいで……閉じてて……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Because... when people exist... to still exist one by one as if solitary islands on distant seas... closed off..."
comments: Tomoki's island, or Yusa's? See above, Gunjou the Island Prison, though laterally it's also the Cross World in a more psychological reading. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri says that even with people present, each person is closed off like an isolated island. The English repeats 'exist' in an ungoverned infinitive and does not form a complete clause.

highlights.text: when people exist... to still exist one by one

adjudicated.jp: 「いやなんです……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "That is just not right..."
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese repeats Kiri's personal 'I don't like it.' The English again substitutes an impersonal judgment that it is wrong.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "......"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: かまってください―――
adjudicated.en: "Care about me, please---"
comments: around Switched. -GHS

adjudicated.jp: まるで霧は、
adjudicated.en: It's just as if Kiri, all along,

adjudicated.jp: そう叫んでいるように見えた。
adjudicated.en: had been shouting that.
comments: And the reason she wants to impose a certain shape of happiness on the world is because she doesn't believe she'll ever attain hers without it. It's why she's so easily convinced to secede, which Taichi reprises when he talks about her "finding a place where she belongs" - but not with weapons. (It's still Heaven tho.) -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「それが君の傷か」

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...eh?'
adjudicated.assessment: The dialogue opens with a double quotation mark but closes with a single quotation mark.

adjudicated.jp: 新川が呻く。
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa groans.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「お、お兄チャマが起きそう」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Oh, looks like Onii-chama's waking up."
comments: OHAIOOOOOO, TAKE IMOTO-SAN TO THE CULTURAL FESTIVAL -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The deliberately childish distortion of 'older brother' is left as an unexplained Japanese kinship form rather than represented in English.

adjudicated.jp: 「豊のこと好きなの？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Do you really like-like Yutaka?"
comments: TOMODACHI-SAN CAME OVER TO, PLAYER WITH IMOTO-SAN -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「それは…………って、な、何言ってるんですかっ」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Well, I...... wait, wh-, what are you talking about?!"
comments: WE ARE PLAYING KAWAI KINGDOM HARTS AND NAR-UHTO. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 赤くなった。
adjudicated.en: She went red.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あっ、だからっ、違いますっ」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Ah! Seriously! Not like that!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「わかりやすい」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "So easy to understand."
comments: Double meaning 'course. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「違いますってばっ」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "It is not like that, I'm telling you!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「いいなあ豊」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Nice, eh, Yutaka."
adjudicated.assessment: いいなあ豊 means that Yutaka is lucky or fortunate. The English instead reads as Taichi telling Yutaka that something is nice.

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...ehhh?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 目をこする。

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "All eaten."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「なん、だと……？」
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "What... the...?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 唖然とする。
adjudicated.en: Mute amazement.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「だって起きるとは思ってなかったから」

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 豊は低く呻いた。
adjudicated.en: Yutaka gave a low moan,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: が、それ以上文句を言う様子はなかった。
adjudicated.en: but outside of that, there didn't seem to be any further complaints.
comments: See Tomoki with regards to Taichi, but not with his sister. More reading key. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Outside of that is an established English idiom meaning apart from or beyond that, not necessarily a spatial description. Together with further complaints, the sentence preserves the source meaning.
adjudicated.remedy: No source-bound correction required; beyond that would be tighter.

adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: かわりに別のことに興味を引かれたようだ。
adjudicated.en: Instead, he seems to have been caught into a different interest.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says something else caught his interest. 'Caught into an interest' is not an English construction.

adjudicated.jp: 俺を見る。
adjudicated.en: He looks at me,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 赤面している霧を見る。
adjudicated.en: he looks at Kiri's red face,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 腕を組んで考える。
adjudicated.en: and he thinks with folded arms.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 豊は再度霧を見あげた。
adjudicated.en: Then Yutaka looked one more time up at Kiri.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ＯＫ、事情はわかった……で、縁談はまとまったのか？」
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "O.K., I get the situation... marriage proposal's all proper and submitted then?"
comments: He's as good as Taichi at this stuff. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 縁談はまとまった asks whether the marriage arrangement has been settled. The English invents submission and does not idiomatically express an arrangement being finalized.

highlights.text: marriage proposal's all proper and submitted then?

adjudicated.jp: 「明日式だ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ceremony's tomorrow."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「しませんっ！！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "It is not!!!"
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri says that she will not do it, in context rejecting the proposed marriage. The English substitutes an impersonal statement that something is not.

adjudicated.jp: そんなことがあった。
adjudicated.en: And that was one of the things that happened.
comments: So in general it was a good day. /end diary -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

withheld.en: Taichi: "One of the food expenses here's asleep."
comments: Can't source 食うブチ as anything but 食いぶち, "a worker's pay". Likely a multiple entendre of the sort that Taichi's used for Yutaka so far, but I don't quite get the pun if so. See CCD0023. Going with Shinkawa being part of the food expense (i.e. a mouth to feed). -GHS
